thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] BGP session instability detected with upstream ProviderDelta (AS64512). Multiple route withdraws observed from SFO egress toward us-east-1. Traffic loss and intermittent DNS failures reported. Triggering P1 pager.

emily: I'm on it. grabbing BGP sessions + checking peering dashboards. Anyone seeing customer impact? :eyes:

raj: seeing withdraws from provider at sfo-edge-router-2. ~30s flaps on a subset of our prefixes (/18s). traceroutes show next-hop timeouts intermittently.

oliver: monitoring from SFO: high packet loss to 198.51.100.0/24. Also seeing NXDOMAIN spikes across our resolver cluster in the same AZ.

emily: started runbook network/bgp-flap (invoked by sre-bot). ordering: verify peering, open ticket with provider, prep alternate path.

sre-bot: Runbook launched: network/bgp-flap. Steps: 1) validate BGP adj; 2) collect bgp routes; 3) apply traffic steering; 4) escalate to NOC.

raj: bgp summary dump:
```text
BGP router identifier 10.0.0.1, local AS 65000
Neighbor        V    AS MsgRcv MsgSent  TblVer  InQ OutQ  Up/Down State/PfxRcd
198.51.100.1    4  64512  18210  18209        0    0    0  00:12:03  0
203.0.113.5     4  64513  18209  18210        0    0    0  00:00:30  120
```

raj: you can see neighbor 198.51.100.1 flapping (low uptime).

oliver: attempting quick mitigation — advertise critical prefixes more aggressively via ProviderEcho (AS64513). applying a route-map to bump localpref for those prefixes so traffic prefers the alternate provider.

emily: agree. Apply for critical customer-facing prefixes and our resolver blocks only. do NOT global more-specifics without approvals.

oliver: applied route-map outbound to 203.0.113.5 (ProviderEcho). verifying propagation and RIB changes now.

emily: support-bot, start customer-impact thread and draft message for status page. Keep it minimal: "Some customers in SFO are seeing increased errors and latency. We're routing around an upstream network issue."

support-bot: Draft posted to internal/status-drafts. Suggest we include affected AZs and an initial ETTF of 30m.

maria: opened INC-2026 with ProviderDelta — ref ticket 987654. Updated status page: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/INC-2026

raj: traceroute from sfo-edge to 198.51.100.45:
```text
1 10.0.0.1 0.35 ms
2 198.51.100.1 * * (flapping)
3 198.51.100.9 1.2 ms
```

oliver: after announcing to ProviderEcho, checks show traffic shifting away from ProviderDelta for the critical prefixes. packet loss dropped from ~8% -> ~0.7% for those prefixes.

emily: good. keep monitoring. can someone ask ProviderDelta to check optics/port errors and hold routing changes while we stabilize?

raj: raised handoff to NOC oncall (Oliver) for overnight. I'll stay on until stable handoff completed.

oliver: acknowledged, taking primary. I'll keep the loop with ProviderDelta and escalate if withdraws resume.

maria: customer comms update sent: short note to impacted customers + link to status. posted to #customers-notified.

support-bot: internal note: classify as "upstream peering outage" and tag SFO, BGP, ProviderDelta.

emily: postmortem owners? raj volunteered to collect route-deltas and timelines; oliver to collect mitigation timeline and config diffs.

raj: saving bgp-change snapshots and exporting to the incident doc.

oliver: final update: currently stable for 22m with alternate path. ProviderDelta acknowledges a hardware flapping issue on their handoff router; they've scheduled a module replacement and will confirm full convergence after replacement.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated — alternate path in place, no wider customer impact observed. Keep channel open for 2h monitoring.

maria: setting ticket state to "monitoring"; will reopen if regressions occur.

support-bot: recommend follow-up in 24h with customers and include resilience actions (secondary sessions, BFD tuning, peering SLA review).

emily: thanks everyone. saving notes into /incidents/2026/bgp-peering-sfo. We'll run a short retro tomorrow.

oliver: thanks all :thumbsup:
